title: Reduce kernel oscillation for decoder multimode workloads
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Context: Over the last month we observed oscillation where the runtime flips between FlashAttention v2 and v3 kernels for long-decoder multimode requests (mixed short/long sequences and streaming-decoding). This produces 10-40 ms tail-latency jitter and occasional decode token regressions for interactive customers. Goal: implement a deterministic, low-cost stabilization layer in the kernel selector + a lightweight runtime probe so we avoid harmful mid-request kernel switches while preserving overall throughput gains from FA3.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Kernel switch backoff prevents >1 switch per request for decoder flows. 2) 90p tail latency reduced by >=15% for affected workloads on canary hosts. 3) No quality regressions measured by existing prompt-eval harness (<=1% diff on top-3 token RER). 4) Feature gated and rolled out via canary with automatic rollback on SLI breach.
work_items: Add per-request kernel affinity token and expiry TTL in runtime router
Implement exponential backoff + min-dwell for kernel changes during prefill->decode transition
Telemetry: emit kernel_decision, reason_code, request_context, time_since_last_switch
Add synthetic mixed-length benchmark to the perf suite and an A/B scenario for streaming decode
Create feature flag (runtime.config.kernel_stabilizer) with override for forced-v2/forced-v3
Write unit tests for selector state machine and integration test on canary cluster
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-stabilizing could keep suboptimal kernel and increase cost. Mitigation: add periodic re-evaluation window with workload-weighted scoring.
Risk: Telemetry increase. Mitigation: sample 5% of low-volume requests; full traces only for failures or canary hosts.
Risk: Regression from FA3 microtiling under certain seq-len distributions. Mitigation: include a fallback fast-path to previous kernel when perf delta < threshold and quality unaffected.
implementation_notes: Selector change should be implemented in kernel_router.cc; add KernelAffinity struct (affinity_id:string, expiry_ns:int64, reason:string) stored on RequestContext
Prefill->decode boundary: enforce min-dwell of 200ms or min-output-tokens=8 (whichever first) before allowing kernel switch
Probe harness: replay 50k real requests from PROD_SAMPLER (anonymized) through the canary runtime and compare token-level timing and logits summary
Guardrail: if 90th-decile decode latency on canary exceeds baseline by >20% we trigger automagic rollback via rollout-controller
PR template: link perf numbers, flamegraphs and quantized walltime comparisons. Include GPU utilization and workspace growth charts.
testing_plan: Unit tests: selector state transitions, TTL expiry, and backoff math
Integration: end-to-end prefill+streaming decode on canary with real workload sampler (50k requests)
Perf: run mixed-length benchmark under 3 batch size distributions and compare v2 vs v3 behavior
Quality: run eval set of 2k prompts, verify top-1/token distribution and token-level logit drift < threshold
Canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with SLO checks after each step (automated)
telemetry_and_dashboards: Alert: decode_90p_latency_ms_canary > baseline*1.20 for 10m -> incident page
Sampling: tag 100% canary requests; sample 5% in prod; dump full traces when reason_code=FAILSAFE
notes_log: 2025-02-25: Triage — multiple customer reports (internal ticket TCK-882) and infra alarms show elevated tail latency during interactive decode. Assigned to Liam.

2025-02-27: Spike — reproduced jitter locally with synthetic mix (short:0-16, long:512+). Observed selector flip on kernel decision when workspace heuristics changed after first decode token. Hypothesis: runtime re-evaluates kernel on decode due to changed seq-length distribution and accepts FA3 which is suboptimal mid-request.

2025-03-01: Design review — proposed min-dwell + TTL affinity approach accepted by runtime leads; trade-off: could delay beneficial switch for long requests. Decided to allow re-eval on explicit scoring improvement >5% net latency savings.

2025-03-02: Implementation — created branch feat/kernel-stabilizer (GH: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2147). Initial selector state machine and tests pushed. Added preliminary telemetry events.

2025-03-03: Canary plan — will enable on canary pool 'south-us-canary' for 5% traffic. Early metrics job will run 6 hours post-deploy and produce perf snapshot. Rollout controller hook created (PR #2159).
next_steps: Finish unit tests and full integration run on canary hosts (Liam)
Review PR with runtime team and SRE (by 2025-03-05)
Run canary for 24h, gather telemetry and compare against baseline, then schedule 25% rollout if metrics good
Document selector algorithm in Confluence and add to runtime playbook for on-call
